Accepted risks: run-backed approval drift, keying on read-view freshness. The Final Report's 'different vendor' is a stated assumption that is false for this round (F4).
Checkpoint removal runs under withGovernanceWriteGuard (ClearCloseoutCheckpoint); the sealed-bundle read is local to one preparation via a lazily filled map; focused tests pass under -race.

Unreadable or incomplete sealed history becomes an explicit plan blocker; a checkpoint that cannot be removed is reported in Unconfirmed and in NextAction with the file to remove (TestAStopWhoseCheckpointCannotBeRemovedSaysSo).
Review plan, bundle lineage and closeout apply remain integrated; the sealed closeout, milestone-review and done-spec integration checks pass.

Ran the 11 focused tests with -race: all pass, covering kept gate/approval, no gain without seal, unreadable history blocker, open spec owes gate, no-checkpoint decision, other stops still record, older checkpoint cleared, removal failure reported.

The cause (plan is an input of the bundle; the done-spec plan dropped the gate, superseding the bundle) is addressed by reading the governing sealed bundle's criteria (D1); the checkpoint defect is addressed by not recording a non-progress stop on a non-current read view (D2).

mappings.rationale: The ADR amendment records D1 (R1, R2): a done sole-member spec keeps the gate criterion only when its governing sealed bundle carries it, and gets a blocker when sealed history is unreadable; it also records D2 (R4, R5): no checkpoint for a stop on an unknown read view of a done scope.

Retaining a criterion only adds a requirement; it is keyed on the sealed plan, so no approval is created or widened; checkpoint removal uses the store path under the write guard; no secrets handled.

D1 rejects the smaller 'add to every done spec' option because it would supersede approvals; D2 avoids recording rather than deleting after the fact. ~80 lines of production code, no new extensibility. Invalidated if a done spec sealed with the gate still reads superseded or a stop's progress cannot be recovered from the repository.

findings.action: Restrict the stop to a verify blocked by the read view (freshness unknown) and keep plan.NextAction for other blockers
findings.rationale: StoppedOnUnstableInputs keys on Freshness != current (wider than R4's 'unknown') and does not check that the read view is what blocked verify; a done scope blocked for another reason under a non-current view is reported as terminal-verification-unstable-inputs with the generic next action instead of plan.NextAction, and keeps no checkpoint (cli/closeout_plan.go:327, :406). Declared as a residual risk in the spec.
